newsitem.title: UK: Bearing Power sees profit below expectations.
newsitem.headline: Bearing Power sees profit below expectations.

text.p: British power transmission component supplier Bearing Power International Plc said on Tuesday that it saw its pre-tax profit for the 1996 financial year below market expectations due to accounting reasons.

"Largely as a result of the company adopting a new accounting method of stock valuation, it is expected that the final results will reflect a profit figure substantially below current expectations," Bearing said in a statement.
Current market expectations of the Bearing Power's pre-tax profit for the financial year ended at September 30, 1996, are between 1.6 million stg and 1.8 million stg, it said.
Bearing Power will announce its results for the financial year on December 6.
Bearing Power said it intended to recommend the payout of an unchanged final dividend of 1.5625 pence per share in the absence of unforeseen circumstances.
At 1048 GMT, Bearing Power shares stood at 16p, down five pence from Monday's close.
